key_insight: A soft robotic hand exoskeleton can restore intentional grasping in people with severe hand impairment. By adding wrist dorsiflexion support and an active opposable thumb, it enables more dexterous, functional movements like feeding.
problem_solved: Severe hand paralysis often leaves people unable to perform everyday grasping tasks, even when some intention to move remains. This paper addresses the need for a lightweight, wearable assistive device that can convert user intent into practical hand function.
method: Built a lightweight textile-based hand exoskeleton designed for comfortable wearability.
Added wrist dorsiflexion assistance to improve hand positioning for grasping.
Integrated an active opposable thumb to increase hand articulation and enable more dexterous grips.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights how human-centered robotics and assistive control can translate intent into meaningful action in real-world settings. It shows the value of combining wearable design, soft robotics, and control systems to improve quality of life for users with severe motor impairment.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of impaired hand vs. assisted grasping

paper_title: A dexterous soft hand exoskeleton restores intentional grasping in individuals with severe hand impairment
paper_authors: John Nassour, Nicolas Berberich, Daniel Utpadel-Fischler, Tobias Wächter, Gordon Cheng
